body:
Served error page — a seventh served stand app whose actions panic, return an error and log, so a cold agent meets
`caused`: its stand checks, a goal in the stand prompt and a count in the verdict (v030-10's reach).

- A seventh served stand app in `examples/seven_guis`, served by the `escher-session` binary beside the six
  (`counter` · `flight-booker` · `timer` · `crud` · `cells` · `load`), whose controls, each by an ordinary driver step,
  make a handler panic, make a handler return an error the root error boundary takes, and make a handler log — so an
  acting call's answer on that app carries `caused`. [inferred] — the entry names "actions panic, return an error and
  log"; which controls, how many, which levels and which acting verbs reach them is the plan's, its forks brought to
  the operator (the operator's directive, relay-1).

- Its stand checks: the app booted headlessly through `seven_guis::stand`, in both layout modes, each control's
  acting call answering the `caused` items it is built to cause, tied to the control's stable id, owner and event; the
  served app listed and reached through the host and the `mcp` role as the other served tasks are. [inferred]

- A goal in the stand prompt of the cold-agent pipe (`scripts/cold-agent.sh`), asking the agent to meet the error
  page and make sense of what its controls cause, phrased once (test-plan's `prompt-goal-control-phrase-once`).
  [inferred]

- A count in the cold-agent verdict (`target/cold-agent/verdict.json`): the calls whose answer carried `caused`, read
  from the live server child's kept checks or transcript as bools and counts only, never the text; and, beside the
  pipe's other required counts, whether the run is required to meet it — the plan's lean against v030-15's
  acceptance, which the next entry («Cold-agent live run») proves. [inferred]

- The pipe's contract tests (`.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py`) and the capability statement pins
  (`docs/capabilities.md`, `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py`) moved where the served-app count or the
  verdict's fields are held. [inferred]

- The founder's F5 «В 0.3.0, до прогона» (option B): a seventh served app, its stand checks, a goal in the prompt, a
  count in the verdict, and the boundary widening the option names — a new served app, and authored error text
  crossing to the model provider in the run. His word covers exactly that and nothing past it (record:
  `escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-18-cold-agent-bar/inputs/I5-cold-agent-bar-founder-2026-11-18.md.txt`; the relay at
  its source, snapped here as this chunk's input). It supersedes the earlier «`caused` out of the run's reach».
- How the page is built is technical: the operator's, brought to him as forks at P4 (relay-1).

- The authored error text — every panic message, `Err` text and log message and field the app writes — carries
  nothing a scrub would redact: no field named in the hidden set (`url` · `href` · `src` · `html` · `text` · `value` ·
  `attrs` · `path` · `request` · `error` · `password` · `panic.payload`), no host path, no secret, no user text, so what
  crosses in `caused` is the app's own fixed text, read in full (relay-1). [inferred] — the scrub set as
  `escher-telemetry` holds it is P3's to read.
- The P5 card says, per control, what an agent reads in `caused` (relay-1).

- The live run is not this chunk's: it fires once, on the founder's F3, in «Cold-agent live run» (`chk-bx26t3rg`),
  which carries `proves v030-15`. This chunk runs no live agent and reaches no model provider.

- No new driver verb, argument, carrier, cause, session error, exit, node key, log field or span; the served-task
  table grows by one entry. [inferred]

- The six served apps' answers stay byte for byte as they are (their kept checks and `stand_cross_os_readings`).
  [inferred]

- The snapshot of the new app stays under `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET`, and its boot reads 0 lint findings, as the lean
  stand screens do. [inferred]

- CARRY (cry-lfxplxbr): the founder's F5 places a served error page in 0.3.0 before the live run — a seventh app, its
  stand checks, a prompt goal and a verdict count, and the boundary widening its option names (a new served app;
  authored error text crossing to the model provider) — superseding the earlier «`caused` out of the run's reach»; no
  ordinary step on the six served apps answers `caused` today (record:
  `escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-18-cold-agent-bar/inputs/I5-cold-agent-bar-founder-2026-11-18.md.txt`).

- [inferred] "no ordinary step on the six served apps answers `caused` today" — a claim of the carry, kept verbatim;
  P3 re-reads it against the stand's code (its handlers' log sites, `panic!` and `Err(`).

- CARRY (cry-72hc55ey): the architecture row `contract/driver-forms/is-select` says `is_select` is read by the
  driver's `locate` alone, while the crate-private `target_of` that reads it is also called from `Session::actions` —
  measured at the 2026-11-18-cold-agent-bar wrap, its fix this entry's wrap (record:
  `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-18T09-02-58-wrap/cascade-dispositions.md`). The fix is a master-row correction the wrap
  lands; the plan names it in Expected amendments. [inferred] — the call sites re-read at P3.

- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/` (the new app) · `src/stand.rs` (its headless boot) · `src/session_host.rs`
  (the served-task table, `TASKS: [(&str, Served); 6]`) · `src/app.rs` (the windowed stand, if the app joins it).

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/` (the stand checks; the blitz-tests target pin `.github/scripts/test_blitz_tests_targets.py`;
  the `stand-repeat` leg's named targets in `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh`).
- `examples/seven_guis/tests/` (the binary's served-task checks).
- `scripts/cold-agent.sh` · `scripts/cold-agent.ps1` · `.github/scripts/test_cold_agent.py` (prompt goal, verdict count).
- `docs/capabilities.md` · `README.md` · `.github/scripts/test_capability_statement.py` (served-app counts).

- Masters: architecture (the stand's served tasks, the verdict's fields), security-plan (the cold-agent crossings:
  the new served app and its authored error text to the provider, on F5), obs-plan (the verdict rows, the `caused`
  record class), test-plan (the stand prompt, the pipe), a11y-plan and design/layout (the new app's screen).

- CI#44279555352 on `e4c8e3047` (the last wrap's commit): in progress at Setup (oldest check Test [default
  features] at 480 s) — verdict not yet available; re-read before the P5 review.

body:
# Cold-agent bar (v030-15) — the founder's answers, 2026-11-18

Given by the founder by dialog in the overseer session, answered by 2026-11-18 07:55Z, and relayed by the
overseer. The forks are the builder's `forks-founder.md` of the phase run `2026-11-18T06-33-34-phase` (F1–F5).
Each answer is his chosen label, verbatim, beside the fork's own option letter. F2 was not asked in this dialog.

## F1 — the wrong-call bar
The question said 0.2.0's run read 66 calls, 0 wrong, $0.82 under his bar «не больше 5 %», that 0.3.0's prompt is
wider than the one that baseline was measured on, that the run would make about 80 to 100 calls and meet new
refusals (`covered` on a closed select's option and under an open list, `malformed` on a `layout` without an id).

The four options: keep 5 % · 0 wrong · tighter than 5 % but above 0 (2 %) · 5 % with the engine's own limits not
counted.

His answer: «Оставить 5 % (Recommended)»

The fork's option A: at most 5 % wrong, the same rule as 0.2.0.

## F3 — the word to run a live fresh agent
The question: may `bash scripts/cold-agent.sh run stand` fire once, through his own Claude Code login, reaching
the model provider; 0.2.0 cost $0.82 at 66 calls under a $3 cap; never in CI or a loop.

The three options: once under the $3 cap · once under a higher cap ($5) · not now.

His answer: «Один раз, лимит $3 (Recommended)»

The fork's option A: one run, once, `--max-budget-usd 3`. It is his word for ONE run. By his F5 answer below, that
run fires only after the served error page exists.

## F4 — graph and actions answers reaching the model provider (a boundary widening)
The question named what would newly cross: in `graph`, stable ids, owner ids, component names, state names,
handler event names, flags; in `actions`, ids, the verb table's words, closed cause words; no control value and no
typed text by construction; the stand's apps only, from the public repository.

The three options: ratify graph and actions · actions only · neither.

His answer: «Утвердить graph и actions (Recommended)»

The fork's option A: the crossing is ratified for `graph` and `actions` answers on the live run; the security row
is restated at the wrap with this word.

## F5 — a served error page, so a cold agent meets `caused`
The question said that on the built binary no ordinary step on the six served apps answers `caused` (v030-10),
that the stand's code holds no log site, `panic!` or `Err(`, and that `caused` is proven today on fixture pages
alone, so a cold agent never meets it; and asked whether a seventh stand app whose buttons panic, return an error
and log should be added.

The three options, as read to him:
- in 0.4.0 (marked recommended): a route entry for the next version, 0.3.0's run names `caused` out of its reach;
- in 0.3.0, before the run: «Новый чанк (или перепланирование этого): седьмое приложение, его проверки на стенде,
  цель в подсказке и счётчик в вердикте. Холодный агент встречает ошибку и должен в ней разобраться. Цена: это
  расширение границы (новое отдаваемое приложение и авторский текст ошибок, уходящий провайдеру), живой прогон и
  закрытие 0.3.0 сдвигаются минимум на чанк.»
- not at all.

His answer: «В 0.3.0, до прогона»

He chose against the marked recommendation. The fork's option B. What the chosen option's own text states, and so
what his word covers: a new chunk or this one re-planned; a seventh served app; its stand checks; a goal in the
prompt; a count in the verdict; and the boundary widening it names — a new served app, and authored error text
crossing to the model provider in the run. The live run and the close of 0.3.0 move behind it.

## F2 — what the run's result may claim (asked in a second dialog, answered by 2026-11-18 08:59Z)
The question: what the README and the capability page say after the live run, on a pass and on a fail; 0.2.0's
README form was quoted beside it; no test pins the run's numbers.

The three options: the run as measured, naming its reach · the outcome and the counts alone · nothing until a
second run repeats it.

His answer: «Измеренное, с досягаемостью (Recommended)»

The fork's option A. As the option read to him: on a pass, the tools (fifteen), the apps, the call and wrong
counts, the bar, and that `graph`, `actions`, `layout`, the list and (by his F5) the error were each used, plus
what the run did not reach and where each is proven (handler coverage, a component alone, the seed, the fonts);
on a fail, the same counts, the reasons, and the heading «built, its cold-agent run failed against the bar» until
a run passes.

## The README's interim heading (the overseer's PROVISIONAL answer of 2026-11-18 04:24Z)
The question quoted the heading «0.3.0 — built, its cold-agent run to come» and the sentence «16 of its 17
capabilities are verified headlessly; a fresh agent's run over the new capabilities is the version's last step»,
said both are pushed (`764b4ba6`), and that by his F5 the heading stands longer than one chunk.

His answer: «Оставить (Recommended)»

The PROVISIONAL mark is discharged by this word: the wording is his.

This overseer's reading, not his words: how the page is built (which controls, what text, one app or a task of an
existing one) is technical and the builder's plan; whether to re-plan the pending chunk or add an entry ahead of
it is a route question settled at the route-resolve; the operator's earlier technical answer «`caused` named out
of the run's reach» is withdrawn by this answer.

body:
- **boot_load / boot_cells** — 27 references in 12 files (query: `refs WHERE callee_name IN ('boot_load','boot_cells')
  AND callee_file LIKE '%seven_guis/src/stand.rs'`): `session_host.rs`, `stand.rs`, `examples/seven_guis/tests/common/mod.rs`,
  and `stand_actions` · `stand_cells_served` · `stand_contrast` · `stand_cross_os_readings` · `stand_explore` ·
  `stand_graph` · `stand_handler_coverage` · `stand_keyboard` · `stand_layout` · `stand_load_page` ·
  `dioxus_runtime_probe`. The served-page tables a seventh boot joins are among them.

- **boot_errors · ErrorPage · Errors** — no symbol holds the names (query 4); `errors` is two unrelated `term`s
  (`wpt/runner`, `blitz-html`). The new names are free.

- **A served page beside the lean four** (`stand.rs:177-220`, `session_host.rs:16-30`): its own `boot_*`, a root in
  `TaskShell`, a `Served` arm and one `TASKS` row; never a `LeanTask` variant (22 `stand_*` files iterate
  `LeanTask::ALL` against four-row tables) and not on the windowed stand's Home (the load page is not).

- **What a step caused is read by the capture, not the sink** (`capture.rs:120-135`, `format.rs:19-34`): a log under
  the app's own target reaches `caused` as `source: app` at every level and is dropped whole by the stderr sink.

- **A panic is accepted** (`execute.rs:740-760`): caught per step, the call `Outcome::Acted`, so it is no wrong call
  in the cold-agent verdict (`wrong_calls` = refused + error span endings + foreign + denials).

- **An app's own boundary keeps the app on screen** (`stand_act_error_text.rs:205-215`): its fallback replaces only its
  children, `boundary: own`; the root boundary replaces the whole app (`stand_act_errors.rs`, own session).

- **The pipe reads answers as JSON from the transcript, counts only** (`cold-agent.sh` `list_opens`): an accepted
  acting answer decoded by `json.loads`, a field's presence counted, nothing of it kept.
- **Signals through the graph hook, writers `const`** (`tasks/counter.rs:7-11`; arch decision/const-declared-writers).

- **CSS in a `const` raw string, the stand accent `#3a5ce5` / `#2a4cd3` / `#1f3fc1`, page `#f5f5f5`, text `#1a1a1a`**
  (`stand.rs:250-296`; layout-templates decision/stand-accent-colour).
- **Every actionable element keyed by an HTML `id` attribute alone** (layout-templates decision/every-stand-control-keyed).

- **A stand check per file, both layout modes, failure messages naming mode and index only**
  (`stand_act_errors.rs:51-53`; test-plan decision/one-test-target-per-behaviour).

- **The pipe's JSON by python's json module, the fake and the pipe moving together** (`cold-agent.sh:37-40`;
  obs-plan decision/harness-json-via-python-json).
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/errors.rs` — the error page's component, its CSS and its controls

- `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_errors_served.rs` — the served error page's stand check: each control's `caused`
  through the session, in both layout modes, and through `serve_mcp`; its boot reading 0 lint findings and a snapshot
  under `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` (`stand_lint` holds the lean four alone: `git grep -n load --
  tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_lint.rs` 0 hits, as the load page's boot lint sits in `stand_load_page`)
- `examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/mod.rs` — `pub mod errors;`

The operator's answers to the P4 forks of 2026-11-18-served-error-page, given by question dialog:

Q: Served error page — what should its controls ask of a cold agent?
A: Goal needs caused (Recommended) — a small order form: a quantity field, Submit and Export; Submit with a bad quantity returns an Err whose fixed text names the rule, the screen showing only a generic failure; a good Submit logs at info and shows "Order placed" (the done state); Export panics with a fixed message.

Q: Which error boundary should take the page's Err?
A: App's own, with Retry (Recommended) — an ErrorBoundary inside the page shows a generic fallback and a Retry that clears it; the app stays on screen; caused reads boundary own.

Q: How should the cold-agent verdict count caused?
A: By kind, each required (Recommended) — caused_by_kind, an object of the three closed words (panic, error, log) to the count of accepted acting answers carrying an item of that kind, read from the transcript; capability-unused fails a run where any kind reads 0.

body:
## 2026-11-18-served-error-page — 6. Log Coverage: 1 row(s)
**Section:** 6. Log Coverage
**Change:** ~ contract/escher-session-exit-codes/2 · promise: was «Usage: one fixed line on stderr built from `VERBS` and the six task names, stdout empty.»; now «Usage: one fixed line on stderr built from `VERBS` and the served task names, stdout empty.»
**Why:** contract/escher-session-exit-codes/2: The row's «six task names» is false now the served-task table holds seven, and fit read the count as code-held inventory, so the row takes the shorter form that names no count.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-18T16-02-11-wrap/

- Stand cue: `stand_flight_booker.rs` asserts the invalid-date cue (`invalid` class + `disabled` Book) without colour; `stand_accessibility_ids.rs` pins each lean task's Tab sequence (`focus_next_node` from the root element) against the shared table `tab_order` in the stand checks' shared module — CRUD's restated since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness to six stops, `back-btn`, `crud-filter`, `crud-list`, `crud-name`, `crud-surname`, `crud-create`, and the flight booker's to four, `back-btn`, `flight-type`, `flight-start`, `flight-book`, the two other tasks' unchanged and asserts the 14 stand controls' roles and non-empty names — and, since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions, that every interactive-role tree node of the four lean tasks reads a non-empty name (the nine roles of `INTERACTIVE_ROLES`; the CRUD list named `People` by `aria-label`), each `REGION_NAMES` row's name in the tree and the snapshot, and that the tree the shell hands the adapter (`Document::accessibility_tree` through `&dyn blitz_dom::Document`) equals `harness.doc.accessibility_tree()` node for node, with the same focus and root, every `author_id` on it the node's `element_id`; `stand_actionable_keys.rs` asserts every actionable element of the lean tasks and Home reads an author key (`DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable()` empty, in every state), with no `tabindex`, role or Tab-order change, and since 2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep the three non-lean tasks too — Temperature Converter · Circle Drawer · Cells 0 · 0 · 0, in both layout modes and with Circle Drawer's dialog open, through nine author ids added by `id:` lines alone (until then 2 · 3 · 676), and the load page the stand serves reads none either (`stand_load_page`); the load page and Cells hold Tab-order, keyboard and contrast rows (`stand_keyboard`, `stand_contrast`, `stand_load_page`, `stand_cells_served`; `LOAD_TAB_ORDER` and `CELLS_TAB_ORDER` in the shared module beside `tab_order` and `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER`; a Tab order reached only after a state change, such as the order page with its failure shown, is stated as a local table of the keyboard check, not in the shared table), so SC 2.1.1 and 1.4.3 are asserted on the load page's `load-fetch` Button and on Cells' `cells-grid`; the elements that react to input and state no interactive role are counted and pinned as measured (`stand_non_lean_tasks`: 0 on the four lean tasks, Home and Temperature Converter, Circle Drawer 1, Cells 677, the 676 data cells and `cells-grid`) — the snapshot field `NodeState.clickable` (`NODE_FIELDS` fourteen) says that an element reacts to a click, read from the vdom walk's current `click` listeners on an element that is no disabled form control and not from the listener mark, that reading measured by `dioxus_runtime_probe`'s link 2 (in both layout modes, in the workspace `test` leg and in neither the `a11y` nor the `stand-repeat` leg), and `stand_non_lean_tasks` asserts a `CLICKABLE` table of the elements that read `clickable` and state no role, in both layout modes — Counter, Temperature Converter, Flight Booker, Timer and CRUD 0 each, Circle Drawer 1, Cells 676 — beside the listener mark's count, Cells 677; since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness SC 2.1.1 on the stand's buttons is met by measurement: `stand_keyboard.rs` reads Enter and Space on each focused stand button as its click (16 rows, `counter-increment`, `flight-book` and `crud-create` changing the screen; a focused single select such as the flight booker's `select#flight-type` instead opens its list on a pressed Enter, or a pressed Space with no typed text standing, and a released Space does nothing more), and through the driver `stand_act_keys.rs` presses `enter` and `space` on a Tab-focused `counter-increment`, each naming `counter-value`; since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions Enter and Space also read as the click of the two buttons enabled after boot, `crud-update` and `crud-delete`, each reached by keyboard alone (4 rows), and the Tab walk is asserted in two enabled states, each reached by keyboard alone, against the shared table `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER` — the flight booker after the return flight is chosen on `select#flight-type` by ArrowDown, five stops; CRUD after a row is selected, eight, `crud-update` and `crud-delete` last — every `controls(task)` id lying in `tab_order` ∪ `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER`.

- A Tab / Shift+Tab key-press focus check exists on the stand (`stand_snapshot_state`, through the harness's `press` / `press_with`; `stand_accessibility_ids` pins the lean tasks' `focus_next_node` sequence); a range-input key and click check runs in both layout modes (`range_input_interaction`, a disabled range taking neither keys nor a click; on the stand `stand_act_range` moves the Timer slider through the driver by click and key, and an arrow step after two Tabs leaves it focused with role `Slider`, its name and the forward focus sequence unchanged); since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness `stand_keyboard` drives Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space and the CRUD list's keys headlessly on the four lean tasks through the same `press` / `press_with`, reading the focused node back per step in both layout modes, and pins the flight booker's `select#flight-type` moving its choice by its arrows (`the_flight_type_select_moves_its_choice_by_its_arrows`) — each task's stated sequence is the shared table `tab_order` (CRUD six stops, `crud-list` third: it takes `tabindex="0"` and an `onkeydown`, ArrowDown / ArrowUp / Home / End moving the selection, its rows not focusable), and through the driver `stand_act_keys` presses `enter` and `space` on a Tab-focused `counter-increment`; since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions the walk is also asserted in two enabled states, each reached by keyboard alone (`enable_by_keyboard`), against the shared table `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER` beside `tab_order` in the shared module — the flight booker after the return flight is chosen on `select#flight-type` by ArrowDown, five stops (its boot `tab_order` four, `back-btn`, `flight-type`, `flight-start`, `flight-book`); CRUD after a row is selected, eight — every `controls(task)` id lying in `tab_order` ∪ `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER`, and Enter and Space read as the click of `crud-update` and `crud-delete` (4 rows), so a control enabled after boot needs its place in `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER`, while a Tab order reached only after a state change, such as the order page with its failure shown, is stated as a local table of the keyboard check, not in the shared table, while the load page and Cells hold Tab-order, keyboard and contrast rows (`stand_keyboard`, `stand_contrast`, `stand_load_page`, `stand_cells_served`) — `stand_keyboard` walks the shared tables `LOAD_TAB_ORDER` and `CELLS_TAB_ORDER`, beside `tab_order` and `ENABLED_TAB_ORDER`, forward and back in both layout modes, the load page's button taking Enter and Space, Cells' arrows and Enter opening the moved-to cell's editor and its value committing by keyboard, Tab leaving an open editor and a click on another cell each committing it, and the arrows clamping at the grid's ends and bringing a cell into view — so SC 2.1.1 and 1.4.3 are asserted on the load page's `load-fetch` Button and on Cells' `cells-grid`; a select key and typeahead check runs in both layout modes — `select_interaction` (18 tests: a 14-row keys table and a 7-row typeahead table, one `input` and one `change` per change and none for no change, `has_changes` asserted per row, the typed text kept for one second of the document's clock, a disabled select taking no key and no click, an app writing `selected` re-seeding the choice) and, through the driver, `stand_act_select` (10 tests: Tab `fx-before` → `fx-pick` → `fx-named` → `fx-after` → `fx-before`, the disabled `fx-off` skipped, equal before and after the choices, an option chosen by a click then a key) — both in the `a11y` leg, both three rounds in the `stand-repeat` leg, `stand_act_select` by its `stand_` prefix and `select_interaction` by the leg's named `--test` list; the select list's keyboard and focus coverage is headless — `select_popup` (25 tests), `stand_act_popup` (12) and `stand_keyboard`'s list walks (`the_flight_type_walk_holds_with_its_list_open_and_after_each_close`, `a_click_opens_the_list_focus_stays_on_the_select_and_the_walk_goes_on_from_it`) assert SC 2.1.1 and 2.4.3 on it in both layout modes, and the windowed list is read and not run. - In the engine and upstream crates `tracing` is gated per call site with a `#[cfg(not(feature = "tracing"))] let _ = …;` fallback; escher-telemetry (no `[features]`) emits its startup and panic events ungated, and escher-driver takes `tracing` with no feature for its spans — the `command` span and, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, the `tool_call` span, the parent of `command` on an MCP tool call — built by hand with `tracing::info_span!` (no `#[instrument]`); an app crate that logs takes `tracing` itself as a workspace dependency, since dioxus-native's prelude re-exports no tracing.

- The wire (`wire.rs`, crate-private, versioned `v3`, `v2` until 2026-10-19-session-recording) is one request line and one reply line per connection: `hello v3` → `ok v3 pid= label= served= idle_expiry_s=`, `stop v3` → `ok v3 stopping`, `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` → `ok v3 accepted <json>` · `ok v3 refused <json>` · `ok v3 oversize` · `ok v3 recording-failed` (sent in place of the answer when the host's recording ended after the call, the client reading it as `RecordingFailed`), another version of a known word → `refused version`, anything else → `refused malformed`. Kinds are `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value are percent-escaped byte for byte and decoded strictly. A request is bounded at 16,384 bytes, a lifecycle reply at 128, an answer at 1,048,576 on its JSON line; each read and write at 2 s, a client's read of an answer at 30 s. **What the screen reads crosses it in an answer** — ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or a file input's as the mask), the snapshot's text and the diff — and an element id and typed text cross in (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10); no `NodeId` crosses.
